question: My AMD GPU is not detected on Linux and the log shows a discovery timeout. What is the cause and the remedy?
answer:
Quotes:
> If your AMD GPU is not detected on Linux and the server logs contain messages like:
> 
> ```
> msg="failure during GPU discovery" ... error="failed to finish discovery before timeout"
> msg="bootstrap discovery took" duration=30s ...
> ```
> 
> This typically means the system's AMD GPU driver is too old. Ollama bundles
> ROCm 7 linux libraries which require a compatible ROCm 7 kernel driver. If the
> system is running an older driver (ROCm 6.x or earlier), GPU initialization
> will hang during device discovery and eventually time out, causing Ollama to
> fall back to CPU.
> 
> To resolve this, upgrade to the ROCm v7 driver using the `amdgpu-install`
> utility from [AMD's ROCm documentation](https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/install-on-linux/en/latest/).
> After upgrading, reboot and restart Ollama. [gpu-01]
Answer: The cause of the AMD GPU not being detected on Linux with a discovery timeout is likely due to an outdated AMD GPU driver. Ollama requires a compatible ROCm 7 kernel driver, and if the system is running an older driver (ROCm 6.x or earlier), the GPU initialization will hang during device discovery and eventually time out, causing Ollama to fall back to CPU.

To resolve this issue, you need to upgrade to the ROCm v7 driver using the `amdgpu-install` utility from AMD's ROCm documentation. After upgrading, reboot your system and restart Ollama.
